topic: Memory Grove cost clarity, smaller nodes, and hover card
currentUserGoal: Fix the misleading case where 7 available GT appeared sufficient for a node labeled Need 5, make tree skill icons smaller, and show details in a card on mouseover.
workCompleted: Clarified that Soft Touch still costs 12 GT: unaffordable overview nodes now show total cost and shortfall as separate lines, for example Cost 12 GT / Short 5 GT at 7 available GT.
Changed prerequisite labels from ambiguous Need wording to explicit Requires wording.
Expanded the right-side insufficient-funds copy to show Cost, Available, and Short values separately.
Reduced Memory Grove overview hex nodes and their icon art while preserving the larger invisible hit targets.
Increased the zoomed icon size in the right-side inspector so overview icons can remain compact.
Restored an in-tree hover card with the memory name, mechanical effect, total price, and ready/shortfall/prerequisite state.
Anchored the hover card in unused upper-right tree space and disabled it on compact layouts so it does not cover nodes or connector lines.
verificationRun: npm run check passed: ESLint, 31 Vitest tests, TypeScript, and Vite production build.
Browser visual check at 1528x1210 confirmed smaller overview nodes, explicit Cost/Short labels, a non-overlapping hover card, and the larger right-side detail icon.
Browser visual check at 1280x720 confirmed the hover card stays above the connector lanes and all node text remains inside the tree panel.
Browser console check reported no warnings or errors.
Temporary browser viewport overrides were reset after verification.
currentGitStatus: Expected after this handoff commit: clean worktree on codex/gameplay-update, three commits ahead of origin/codex/gameplay-update.
knownIssues: Soft Touch still costs 12 GT. A run paying 7 GT intentionally leaves the player 5 GT short; whether the first run should always afford a memory is a separate balance decision.
The in-tree hover card is hidden on compact layouts, where the stacked detail inspector remains the information surface.
The user still needs to confirm the smaller overview scale feels right with their own mouse and display scaling.
nextRecommendedSteps: Have the user repeat the 7-GT dormancy case and verify the node now reads Cost 12 GT / Short 5 GT and the hover card feels clear.
Decide explicitly whether a normal first run should guarantee one affordable starter memory; if yes, tune Soft Touch cost or first-run payout rather than disguising the shortfall in UI copy.
Continue with second-tier Memory Grove content only after the starter-purchase pacing decision is settled.
doNotRevert: Do not return to bare Need X labels for unaffordable memories.
Keep overview icons compact and preserve the large zoomed inspector icon.
Keep hover/focus mirrored through the accessible DOM bridge.
Keep the hover card outside connector lanes and hidden on compact layouts.
